programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie tracks down some fast, fresh and easy recipes, featuring tasty minty pea tortiglioni and gnocchi with roasted tomato sauce and rocket pesto.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie visits Basilicata in search of some old school Italian recipes and meets a family of shepherds and an 89-year-old macaroni master.

programme.title: World's Most Secret Hotels
programme.desc: Exploring unique and unusual hotels in Uruguay, Sweden, Scotland, Oman and the Netherlands; a camouflaged fort-like resort perched on the edge of a mountain.

programme.desc: The team discovers hidden retreats in Canada, Iceland, Sweden and the U.K., from sunken hotels to retreats surrounded by lava fields and a compound with military history.

programme.title: World's Most Secret Hotels
programme.desc: Exploring the Scottish wilderness in search of spaceships, and the Welsh mountains to probe some mysterious-looking spheres.

programme.title: World's Most Secret Hotels
programme.desc: The team explores unusual hotels in Uruguay, Sweden, Scotland, Oman and The Netherlands, from a fort-like resort to an isolated hotel.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie heads to Greece, to the island of Skopelos, starting on the mainland in Thessaloniki. Inspired by meze plates and traditional island cuisine he cooks up a smoky aubergine flatbread and a lemony chargrilled chicken with tzatziki and rice.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie heads to Marseille in the south of France. Inspired by their stunning seafood, the traditional flavors of Provence, and the multicultural dishes being served up there, he cooks up a steak with a twist and a sublime courgette and olive tart.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie explores Tunisia to meet traditional couscous makers, eat delicious street food, and get invited to cook with local chefs on a beach. Inspired by everything he sees, Jamie cooks crispy prawn parcels and a chicken and merguez sausage stew.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie's soaking up inspiration in Spain with tapas, flavor-charged rice dishes, and spectacular seafood. He cooks a stunning pork chop with peppers and aioli and a surf and turf skewer of prawns, mushrooms, and local ham.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Corsica, the Island of Beauty, is best explored by railway; from Mediterranean waters to towering peaks, stops include Algajola for a seaside dive, Vizzavona on the GR20 trail and historic cities like Corte with its citadel.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Cinque Terre Express runs along Italy's northern coast east of Genoa; passing through five UNESCO-listed villages, it offers coastal views and access to cobbled streets, harbors, terraced vineyards and pastel-colored houses.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: The Little Yellow Train winds through the Eastern Pyrenees, crossing the Cerdan plateau, the historic Gisclard railway suspension bridge and the Grandes Canalettes caves, known as the underground Versailles of the Pyrenees.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: In Greece, the Intercity Express travels from Thessaloniki to Athens, passing sites like the Meteora peaks, Delphi ruins and the Acropolis; the journey continues to the Peloponnese on Greece's last cogwheel train.

programme.title: Europe's Greatest Train Journeys
programme.desc: Andalusia, now crossed by high-speed and modernized rail lines, unveils its rich culture and landscapes; along the journey, we visit cities like Seville, Granada with its famed Alhambra and Guadix near the Tabernas Desert.

programme.title: Rosas blancas para mi hermana negra

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.desc: An introduction to secret societies; the personal experience of Professor Spence in his hometown of Taft, California; many cults are demonized by their enemies and misunderstood by outsiders; they become the stuff of myths and conspiracy theories.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.sub-title: Secret Societies: The Underworld of History
programme.desc: Rhoads is 16 when she dies; the discovery of her body five years after her death opens the door to public awareness of the Divine Order of the Royal Arms of the Great Eleven; Professor Spence highlights that secret societies come in many forms.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.desc: The Knights Templar is a military monastic order founded during the Crusades; the knights endure through time to become the subject of much rumor and outright fantasy; knowing whether they are guardians for a holy bloodline or devil worshipers.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.sub-title: Masonic Revolutions in America and France
programme.desc: Professor Spence looks at the secret societies behind the Boston Tea Party and Bastille Day; the roles that the Sons of Liberty and others play in these important revolutions; Benjamin Franklin and other founders are involved with secret groups.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.desc: Learning whether the Bolsheviks are a secret society; surveying the rich history of governmental secret societies who combat revolutionary conspiracies; the allure of the elite and the power of conspiracy; the role of a well-oiled secret society.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.sub-title: Adolf Hitler and the Thule Society
programme.desc: The smaller secret societies pop up all over Germany at the end of the 19th century; the larger societies and individuals weave through the background of Hitler's rise to power; the Nazi leader embraces secret-society methods for his own purposes.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.desc: The 1930s see an economic crisis, Hitler's rise, Stalinist terror and the general decline of democracy; knowing whether there is a hidden hand at work undermining democratic institutions and encouraging dictatorship; movements tied to Synarchy ideas.

programme.title: The Real History of Secret Societies
programme.desc: The Eleusinian Mysteries are among the most famous of the Greco-Roman world; this secret society endures for almost 2,000 years; its members include the likes of Socrates, Plato, Plutarch and Cicero; Spence considers if secret societies ever die.

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.sub-title: The Unknown Story of Ancient North America

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.desc: Exploring the very first American culture, which is identified by a specialized hunting tool called the Clovis point; how the Clovis populated the Americas from coast to coast; how some of the Clovis people evolved into the last Paleo-Indians.

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.desc: How Paleo-Indian culture began to diversify regionally; understanding why some groups developed a hunting and gathering culture, while others fished from temporary camps; what DNA research reveals about one ancient sedentary people.

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.desc: How the creative yet disparate peoples of North America developed innovations such as corn agriculture, permanent houses and religion about 5,000 years ago; exploring the only innovation common to these many different cultures.
